subject.title: Add plan-first Claw status and remove

question: After the package race is fixed, should OpenClaw sponsor this full destructive Claws lifecycle—including permanent session/workspace cleanup, retained tombstones, doctor recovery, and the stacked ownership schema—as the core RFC direction?
rationale: The implementation can close the concrete concurrency defect, but code review cannot decide the permanent destructive-state, audit, recovery, and upgrade guarantees for this experimental core feature.

options.title: Sponsor the full lifecycle
options.body: Require shared package serialization, a redacted removal tombstone, doctor recovery semantics, and explicit stacked upgrade proof before landing the complete status/remove surface.

options.title: Land read-only status first
options.body: Split out authoritative status and orphan inventory while deferring destructive removal until its audit and recovery contract is settled.

options.title: Pause the core stack
options.body: Keep the RFC and dependent PRs open without landing until maintainers confirm that grouped Claws belong in core and commit to the persistence lifecycle.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the full lifecycle
recommendation.body: Require shared package serialization, a redacted removal tombstone, doctor recovery semantics, and explicit stacked upgrade proof before landing the complete status/remove surface.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ownership of the shared state/configuration boundaries makes this person the strongest available routing candidate for the permanent lifecycle and recovery decision.
